standard_prerequisites.name: The criterion for a Noetherian ring to be J-1
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the statement that is verified at each regular prime.

standard_prerequisites.name: Elements generating the maximal ideal of a regular local ring form a regular sequence
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-regular-ring-CM}, cited at proof lines 11629-11631
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the regular sequence in the localisation.

standard_prerequisites.name: A regular sequence can be spread out to a neighbourhood
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-regular-sequence-in-neighbourhood}, cited at proof lines 11632-11634
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows replacing the ring by a localisation in which the chosen elements form a regular sequence and generate the prime.

standard_prerequisites.name: A local ring is regular when it is the quotient of a regular local ring by a regular sequence
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-regular-mod-x}, cited at proof lines 11642-11644
standard_prerequisites.use: Concludes regularity at the prime in question.

core_obligations: Choose a regular prime and elements generating it after localisation (proof lines 11626-11628).
Use regularity of the local ring to see that those elements form a regular sequence, and spread the property out (proof lines 11629-11634).
For a prime above it with regular quotient, use the J-0 hypothesis to find such primes in a nonempty open subset (proof lines 11635-11639).
Conclude regularity of the local ring at that prime by the quotient criterion (proof lines 11640-11644).
proof_roadmap: Set up the criterion at a regular prime (proof lines 11624-11628).
Spread out the regular sequence (proof lines 11629-11634).
Find a good prime above and conclude regularity (proof lines 11635-11644).
difficulty_reason: The lemma derives the J-1 property of a Noetherian ring from the assumption that the quotient by every prime is J-0. The proof verifies the applicable criterion at a regular prime: it chooses elements generating the prime after localising there, notes that they form a regular sequence in the localisation because the local ring is regular, spreads that regular sequence out to a neighbourhood by the openness of the regular sequence property, and then uses the J-0 hypothesis to find, among the primes above, one where the quotient is a regular local ring. Regularity of the ring at that prime then follows from the quotient-by-a-regular-sequence criterion.
